questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Their course catelouge was the easiest to navigate of the universities i checked, which made it a lot easier to see if there were any courses i would be interested in taking (there was). I had never been to Amsterdam/the netherlands before, so it was guarenteed to be a new experience. But the culure is also somewhat similar to at home, one of the main benefits for me being that i could still travel by bike around the city, which i'm used to doing at home.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a great experience, but i will say that for me what shaped my good experience the most was not the place or the university. It was the people i've met and spent my time with, that really shaped my experience abroad to what it was.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Overall pretty ok, the university was fairly good at sending out information of what we needed to do, like registering at the municipality. More course specific information was harder to find and was a bit of a challenge.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were some intro days you could sign up for organised by ESN, there were some information but it was mostly just experiencing the city and meeting other exchange students. Then I also had a intro meeting at science, where they gave a bit of information in general about living in amsterdam, but most helpfully study related information like how to navigate the building and where to find your schedule.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Overall good, i was missing a bit more course specific information and i've had a bit of a hard time knowing where to go or who to talk to when i have specific questions.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Found housing through the university

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: can't think of anything, but i also live of campus at home, so this was not new to me.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university does not have housing for everyone and what you get varies both in distance from campus and in what it's like. I didn't live super close, but i really liked the place i lived in.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall easy, however, not once but twice did i not receive an email i was supposed to receive, which ended up significantly delaying the entire process, which made it quite stressful. It is however my impression that i have been very unlucky in this regard.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It's mostly one step, you have to apply, which involves sending your transcript of records, id, courses you are currently taking and informing them of which courses you want to take. After that i got accepted, they checked if i qualified to take the courses and then they signed me up for the courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They have an email for exchange science at the university, where you can ask if you have any problems or questions (which i did very much end up using)

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got registered for the classes i had indicated i wanted on my application.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I was not aware of this when i applied, but if you are a bachelor student, you are only allowed to take bachelor course, which there is a fairly small selection of in english (at least that was the case at science). Also they need the official transcript of records which i couldn't figure out how to get, but it's aquired through student service.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Similar to UCPH i didn't think the level of the material was much diffrent than UCPH, but it does seem to me like the requirements for getting a passing grade are higher than i'm used to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I struggled with it. I encountered more presentation and more researching scientific articles than i'm used to from UCPH, which personally was a challenge just cause i wasn't used to it. On the other hand i encountered fewer excercises and less assigned reading than a UCPH, which i personally missed, but that of course depends on preferences.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Functional materials, Organometalic chemistry, Green and industrial chemistry, Artificial Photosynthesis and Solar Fuels  and Literature research project

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There were both good and bad things about all of the courses i took, my personal favourites were Organometalic chemistry and literature research project though. Organometalic chemistry is exactly what it sounds like, also had a teaching style that more closely resembles UCPH in my opinion which i liked. Literature research project is somewhat more independent course, the goal is to write a project related to a scientific paper (you have a say about the topic), but my favourite thing about the course were the lectures on academic english, it's not a lot of hours, but it's really helpful to pinpoint some of the common mistakes in academic english and how to fix them and i think these classes are really something i am going to bring forward with me and use for all my papers in english from now on. Main downside is that a lot of the course information is in dutch, but i believe that's something they planning on fixing in the future.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had some taxes that weren't covered by the student housing (because some students may be eligible to not pay those taxes, but that wasn't the case for me). Also needed to by things like pots, apns and plates, and a used bike to get around.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I think food was overall slightly less expensive than at home. Nothing was particularly surprising to me though pricewise.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were atheletic oppertunities presented to us, which i didn't end up using. Otherwise the ESN organises some activities, but none of those really interested me either. I got included ina whatsapp group where the chemistry student associasion announces different events, but the messages were in dutch, so i often couldn't be bothered to translate to figure out what they said. Overall there were definetely oppertunities, but nothing i found particularly interesting. I think if you like bars and parties or athletic activities you may have a better chance than me though.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There's a fitness center type building that offers a bunch of classes, but you can also just come on your own. The ESN organises some trips, and cultural events and a lot of meet-ups at a bar. The chemistry student association, organised some chemistry related trips, a few parties and then there was like a weekly meet-up/hang-out/drinking situation. CREA also offers some creative classes (unclear on how closely related they are to the university)

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I mostly just hung out with friends and didn't really use the options, so i have no recommendations.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the city, it's a very nice place to just walk around in.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, amsterdam is similar to copenhagen. My main struggle was being punctual enough. When the schedule says class from 9-10, it's means the lacturer started talking at 9 and you should have been there by now.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I had a hard time with this, most of the other students have known each other for a while and prefer to speak dutch. My main recommendation is to go to the student association events or meet-ups, that's where i interacted most with the local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Mostly the being on time thing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Biking, i liked that a lot. I have also had a good time trying different dutch foods.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get a bike it's the easiest way to get around. Mastercard or visa doesn't always work, so either get a dutch bank account or make sure to carry cash around just in case. Other international students are the easiest to befriend.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be on time for classes.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: For me it's been the trying new things and making new friends. I think being in a new place where you know no one really encourages you to just do stuff and try thing.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding the information i needed about my courses, and adjusting to the different structure of how they do things with courses. For me it felt a little bit like being a confused first year student at university again, except no one else was as confused as me this time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
